card.name: Locking
card.tagline: Los Angeles, 1969 — Don Campbell froze mid-move, and the freeze became a vocabulary.
card.profile: Locking is a style of funk dance. The name is based on the concept of locking movements, which means freezing from a fast movement and "locking" in a certain position, holding that position for a short while and then continuing at the same speed as before. It relies on fast and distinct arm and hand movements combined with more relaxed hips and legs. The movements are generally large and exaggerated, and often very rhythmic and tightly synced with the music.
card.insight: Locking was invented in 1969 by Don 'Campbellock' Campbell in Los Angeles, who originated the freeze-and-point move on Soul Train; the Lockers (Toni Basil, Fred Berry) made it a national phenomenon by 1973.

steps.name: Muscle lock
steps.description: Cross arms in front of the upper body and bring them up.

steps.name: Locking with the hands
steps.description: Bend the left knee and shift the hip to the right side.

steps.name: Uncle Sam
steps.description: Left arm goes down, right hand comes to the left shoulder, and point to the sky.
